marta_support: Escalation from Acme — customer sees repeated partial outputs and duplicate token billing when their client reconnects very quickly (<200ms) after a heartbeat. Correlation ID: cid=acme-2026-03-15-77. Repro steps below. Can someone triage? @ivan_runtime @kai_ml

marta_support: Repro (python):
```python
# simple loop that force-reconnects on purpose
import time, requests
for i in range(3):
    r = requests.get(\"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=fast\", stream=True, headers={\"Authorization\":\"Bearer token\"})
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line:
            print(line.decode())
    time.sleep(0.15)  # reconnect fast
```

marta_support: Repro (node):
```js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
function hackyReconnect(){
  const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=fast', {headers:{Authorization:'Bearer token'}});
  es.onmessage = e => console.log(e.data);
  setTimeout(()=>{ es.close(); hackyReconnect(); }, 150);
}
hackyReconnect();
```

ivan_runtime: Thanks, looking. Can you paste the server-side correlation id from the customer's request logs (we want the x-rw-cid and request-id). Also, did they include Last-Event-ID or any session header?

marta_support: Got logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21.123Z] cid=acme-2026-03-15-77 req=R8f2 ServeStream start kv_cache=hot session_id=acme-42
[2026-03-15T12:03:21.190Z] cid=acme-2026-03-15-77 req=R8f2 heart=ok sent_chunk=tok_1
[2026-03-15T12:03:21.305Z] cid=acme-2026-03-15-77 req=R8f3 reconnect session_id=acme-42 last_evt_id=
[2026-03-15T12:03:21.310Z] cid=acme-2026-03-15-77 req=R8f3 ServeStream start kv_cache=stale replay_prefix=tok_1
```

ivan_runtime: Huh — last_evt_id is empty and we see kv_cache=stale on the reconnect. Looks like the reconnecting client triggers a new ServeStream that replays the prefix token because the cache wasn't marked flushed. If they reconnect quickly we reinitialize a socket and re-send prefix. That can cause duplicate tokens billed and partial outputs when the client drops mid-chunk.

kai_ml: This matches a regression introduced in the KV flush change (rollout 2026-03-12) that optimized synchronous cache eviction. Edge-case: if reconnect happens before the flush finalizer runs, new stream will treat cache as stale and replay previously-sent tokens. Suggests fixes:
- honor SSE Last-Event-ID on reconnect and map to token offset
- require client-provided session id + seq to be accepted as authoritative for dedupe
- short term, throttle immediate replay when reconnect delta < 500ms

ivan_runtime: Agreed. I'll open a hotfix: if last_evt_id empty and reconnect delta < 500ms, we won't start replay, we'll instead skip prefix resend and rely on KV cache async confirmation. Also add a guard to mark kvcache as \"in-flush\" so new sessions don't assume stale. Will add unit tests reproducing quick reconnect.

sourav_eng: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/6218 — labelled hotfix. It adds Last-Event-ID mapping and a 500ms debounce for replay, plus an opt-in header `X-RW-SESSION-ID` to allow SDKs to send stable session ids for safe resume. Also added an integration test that simulates <200ms reconnects.

marta_support: Nice. Customer asked about billing impact — they saw ~120 extra tokens billed across a burst. Can we proactively credit?

ivan_runtime: Yes, please issue a one-time credit for the incident; file an incident note referencing cid=acme-2026-03-15-77 and PR 6218. I'll monitor rollout to staging then prod.

marta_support: Will notify Acme and recommend a temporary client-side workaround: exponential backoff (>=300ms) before reconnect OR set `X-RW-SESSION-ID` to keep the server resume stable. Also to confirm: update SDKs to set Last-Event-ID when reconnecting if available to avoid replay.

kai_ml: We'll also add an SDK test to ensure the JS/Python wrappers send Last-Event-ID and session id on reconnect; ticket added to devex board.

marta_support: Thanks all — closing thread for now, will re-open if customer sees recurrence after the hotfix. :thumbsup:
